## Divisible by 19

### Problem
Given that $x$ and $y$ are integers, prove that $2x + 6y$ is divisible by 19 if and only if $5x - 4y$ is divisible by 19.

### Solution (adapted from the official solution)
**Proof.**

Let $x, y \in \mathbb{Z}$.

### 1. Coprime

$$
\gcd(2, 19) = \gcd(5, 19) = 1.
$$

### 2. Difference

$$
5(x + 3y) - (5x - 4y) = 5x + 15y - 5x + 4y = 19y.
$$

$$
\therefore\ 5(x + 3y) \equiv 5x - 4y \pmod{19}.
$$

### 3. Equivalence

$$
\begin{aligned}
19 &\mid (2x + 6y) \\
\iff 19 &\mid 2(x + 3y) \\
\iff 19 &\mid (x + 3y) \\
\iff 19 &\mid 5(x + 3y) \\
\iff 19 &\mid (5x - 4y).
\end{aligned}
$$

$$
19 \mid (2x + 6y) \iff 19 \mid (5x - 4y)
$$

$$
\therefore\ \text{Proved.}\quad \blacksquare
$$

### Conceptual Explanation
Using [modular arithmetic](#node/node-modular-arithmetic/sec-modular-arithmetic-core), since $\gcd(2, 19) = 1$, $19 \mid (2x+6y) \iff 19 \mid (x+3y)$. The linear difference $5(x+3y) - (5x-4y) = 19y$ establishes $5(x+3y) \equiv 5x-4y \pmod{19}$. Since $\gcd(5, 19) = 1$, $19 \mid (x+3y) \iff 19 \mid (5x-4y)$.

### Key Technique
[Modular arithmetic linear combination](#node/node-modular-arithmetic/sec-modular-arithmetic-core) and coprime reduction using $\gcd(2, 19) = \gcd(5, 19) = 1$.
